correctness.summary: For nu<1/2 the source orthant Skorokhod map gives a unique canonical regulator solution for every continuous boundary. Tanaka's formula plus occupation density shows that zero Stieltjes variation on the contact set is sufficient for regulator=half local time, and for increasing boundaries the same identity makes that condition necessary. At deterministic contact times the regulator equation bounds backward Brownian increments by max{1,1-nu} times the boundary's upward increment; the backward Brownian LIL therefore yields the variation-a.e. sufficient condition. The 1/2-Holder and absolutely continuous corollaries follow directly.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Wang (2026) proves well-posedness under the stronger uniform o(sqrt(h)) condition and counterexamples below Holder exponent 1/2, while separately using the orthant regulator construction for nu<1/2. Searches found no explicit contact-measure equivalence, variation-a.e. LIL refinement, critical 1/2-Holder closure, or modulus-free absolutely continuous corollary for this moving-boundary maximum-perturbed equation. The contact criterion is close to ingredients already in Wang's proof, so the novelty claim is deliberately narrow.

value.summary: The result closes the missing critical Holder endpoint for all subcritical perturbations and shows that uniform roughness is not the true obstruction: every locally absolutely continuous boundary works without a modulus restriction, including t^alpha for alpha<1/2, while the source's failures are singular. The contact-measure formulation isolates the mechanism that distinguishes the two cases.

limitations: Continuous deterministic boundaries of locally finite variation only.
Necessity of zero contact Stieltjes mass is stated only for increasing boundaries.
The variation-a.e. LIL criterion is sufficient; the equality case is unresolved.
The nu>=1/2 critical-boundary regime is not settled.
Independent audit has not been performed.
